outcome: Changes in pregnancy outcomes in HIV-infected women over three decades
Risk factors for severe small-for-gestational-age (SGA) infants
cohort: 262 HIV-infected pregnant women who delivered at the University of Genoa and IRCCS San Martino-IST in Genoa between 1985 and 2014
finding: Significant changes in demographic, clinical and therapeutic characteristics of HIV-infected pregnant women have occurred over the last 30 years, including a decrease in mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) to zero since 2000 and an increased risk of preterm delivery associated with advancing maternal age and previous pregnancies.
mod_finding: Elective caesarean section rates increased from 9.1% in 1985-1994 to 92.3% in 2004-2015, however mode of delivery was not independently associated with preterm delivery.
